ana: Heads-up: offline replay (trace id 195432) shows a regression after we raised the prefetch_threshold to 256 tokens. p95 latency up ~12% on long-seq workloads (seq=2048). full replay log: https://internal.replay/195432

devon: link works for me. is this the offline A/B harness you ran against the same trace?

ana: yes — same trace, split 50/50 between threshold=128 (control) and 256 (experiment). replay-bot posted the summary later.

sandeep: which metric moved exactly? p95 generation or end-to-end RPC?

ana: p95 end-to-end (client->first-token) and kernel queueing visible in timeline. p50 roughly flat.

maggie: quick profiler notes: when threshold=256 I see more frequent KV cache misses during early tokens which forces extra KV warmup work mid-batch. SM utilization is slightly higher but with more stalls. I captured a flame for one sample.

maggie: snippets from perf: `kernel_selector` oscillating between matmul_fused and matmul_split for the same batch sizes, adds ~1.4ms per call due to rebind. L1 load misses spike at the 2nd token in many samples.

ana: replay-bot: can you paste the A/B numbers here?

replay-bot: A/B Summary (trace 195432): control(pre=128): throughput=12.8k tok/s, p95=42ms; experiment(pre=256): throughput=13.6k tok/s, p95=47ms (+12.0%). Token budget target set to 0.6 in both runs. KV-prefetch hit rate: control=87%, experiment=79%.

devon: interesting — throughput improved but p95 worsened. sounds like batching increased but at cost of tail latency when KV warmup misses happen mid-batch.

sandeep: can you paste the config used for the replays? would like to sanity-check token_budget vs prefetch interplay.

ana: config snippet used in experiment run:

```
prefetch_threshold: 256
token_budget_target: 0.6
queue_policy: deadline_weighted
batch_formation: continuous
kv_warmup_cohorting: enabled
kernel_rebind_timeout_ms: 8
```

maggie: that kernel_rebind_timeout_ms of 8 is suspiciously low — rebind thrashing could happen if selector is jittery. we added a small heuristic last sprint to prefer previously-bound kernels for X ms; maybe this is not catching the case where sequence length distribution within a batch fluctuates.

ana: I also noticed in the trace that many requests start short but then extend (streaming/append) which increases sequence lengths mid-batch; combined with larger prefetch we pack more heterogeneous seqs together. kernel selection prefers different kernels and we get thrash.

devon: proposed quick experiments:
- lower prefetch to 192 and run same trace A/B vs 128
- increase kernel_rebind_timeout_ms to 32 in a run to measure bind stability impact
- set token_budget_target to 0.55 and 0.65 to see sensitivity

sandeep: +1. also try enabling a conservative queue heuristic that groups by estimated final seq_len instead of initial. we have that estimator in the trace-harness already.

replay-bot: Queued experiments:
- exp-195432-a: pre=192, token_budget=0.6, rebind=8
- exp-195432-b: pre=256, token_budget=0.6, rebind=32
- exp-195432-c: pre=256, token_budget=0.55, rebind=8
expected runtime ~30m each. will post when done.

ops-bot: FYI: CI regression alert (perf-p95) snoozed for this trace group while we iterate.

maggie: also added a quick kernel_selector debug flag to the harness to emit kernel_score values; the score currently is: `score = alpha * matmul_cost + beta * memory_pressure - gamma * reuse_priority`. attaching a tiny CSV sample from one run: matmul_cost jumps by ~3x for split path on seq>=1024.

ana: thanks. next actions: devon, can you own exp-195432-a? sandeep, please take exp-195432-b and check bind logs. maggie, leave the selector debug enabled for all runs. I'll watch p95 and kv-prefetch hit rate.

devon: on it. kicking exp-195432-a now. ETA 35m. :thumbsup:

sandeep: starting exp-195432-b. I'll also capture PTX sample around the thrash windows.

maggie: will keep selector debug on. If we confirm rebind stability fixes p95, we should consider increasing the default rebind timeout and adding a lightweight cohorting rule for streaming appends.

ana: agreed. will reconvene after results and decide whether to roll a short-term config change vs deeper kernel selection logic change. thanks all. :rocket:
